But note that the claim that bliss does not provide positive well-being (that is, that bliss is not good for the person) is a substantive evaluative claim. This claim, which Classical Utilitarianism rules out, is part of the package of normative and evaluative ideas that the counter-example targets. Bliss versus Torture does not refer to positive and negative well-being; it only refers to bliss, pinpricks, and torture.
